subject: mathematics
title: Visual Percentages & Proportions
summary: A percentage ("per hundred") tells how many parts we take out of 100 equal parts, linking fractions, decimals, and proportional scales.
visualInteractiveHint: Slide the percentage and total value to watch the 0%–100% bar and proportional quantity scale together in real time.
workedExampleTitle: Two visual ways to find 25% of 80

workedSteps.title: Step 1: See the percentage as a fraction out of 100
workedSteps.explanation: 25% means 25 out of 100. Simplifying 25/100 by 25 shows that 25% is always 1/4 of the whole.

workedSteps.title: Step 2: Split the total into 4 equal quarters
Step 3: Alternative method using 10% building blocks

whyItWorks: A proportion keeps the ratio between part and whole constant: 20 out of 80 is the exact same ratio as 25 out of 100.

commonMistake.wrongExample: Common trap: assuming 25% of 80 is just 25.
commonMistake.correction: 25% only equals 25 when the total is 100. When the total is 80, 25% is one-fourth of 80, which is 20.

deepDiveExtra: To calculate any percentage mentally, find 10% first (divide by 10) and 1% (divide by 100), then combine them.

quickChecks.question: If 10% of 60 is 6, what is 30% of 60?
